_activity: Build the thesis: Worcester v. Georgia, 1832
intro: Build the sentence. Drag the correct piece into each blank.
source_document: Document 7 - Chief Justice John Marshall, Worcester v. Georgia, 1832
source_text: . . . The Cherokee nation, then, is a distinct community occupying its own territory, with boundaries accurately described, in which the laws of Georgia can have no force, and which the citizens of Georgia have no right to enter, but with the assent [agreement] of the Cherokees themselves, or in conformity with treaties, and with the acts of congress. . . .
_pointer: Worcester v. Georgia, 31 U.S. 515 (1832), opinion of Marshall, C.J.; Legal Information Institute, law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/31/515, checked 2026-10-15. Gloss ours.

tiles.text: the Supreme Court sided with Cherokee sovereignty over Georgia's claims
Georgia wanted Cherokee land after gold was found there
the Cherokee were forced west on the Trail of Tears
Marshall ruled that Georgia's laws “can have no force” on Cherokee land
gold had been found on Cherokee land in 1829
about 4,000 Cherokee died on the way west

correct_sentence: Document 7 shows that the Supreme Court sided with Cherokee sovereignty over Georgia's claims, because Marshall ruled that Georgia's laws “can have no force” on Cherokee land.
rationale: The gold discovery is historical context, not Marshall's reasoning. The death toll on the Trail of Tears is an effect of what happened after this ruling, not part of it.
